stories.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams has moved on from 4-INT game, but frustration lingers
stories.summary: Caleb Williams spent his bye week resting his ailing hamstring, supporting his close friend Pete Crow-Armstrong as the Cubs outfielder was named NL MVP, and putting one of the worst games of his career in the rearview mirror.
stories.detail: LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Caleb Williams spent his bye week resting his ailing hamstring, supporting his close friend Pete Crow-Armstrong as the Chicago Cubs outfielder was named National League MVP , and putting one of the worst games of his career in the rearview mirror. The Chicago Bears went into their Week 10 bye with a 7-2 record after scraping by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a 27-24 win. Williams found redemption after throwing a career-worst four interceptions against Tampa Bay by leading his first winning drive of the season to set up Cairo Santos for a 38-yard field goal as time expired. Though the quarterback said he has moved past the interceptions, two of which he dubbed "funky" while calling another a "bad decision," the impact of his performance stayed with him during the time away. "The biggest thing is, the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me, personally, I always don't want to let my teammates down," Williams said. "That's always big for me. And in that situation, in those situations, I feel like I did. And so, that's the frustrating part that lingers." Williams' four-interception performance was an aberration over his three-year career. stories.title: Pair of ex-Seahawks safeties find new teams
stories.summary: D’Anthony Bell and A.J. Finley will be heading to new practice squads entering Week 11.
stories.detail: A pair of former Seattle Seahawks safeties have made their way onto practice squads elsewhere, including someone who started on late notice earlier in the season. According to Tuesday’s NFL transaction wire, A.J. Finley signed with the Pittsburgh Steelers practice squad, having been released last week by Seattle. Finley was on injured reserve last season with a torn ACL suffered in training camp, and alternated between active roster and practice squad to start this year. He started in place of the injured Julian Love in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders, played exclusively special teams in Week 4 vs. the Los Angeles Chargers, but hasn’t had any playing time since then. Meanwhile, D’Anthony Bell has joined the Minnesota Vikings practice squad after remaining a free agent after the Seahawks let him go at the end of September. Bell was part of Seattle’s PS and active roster throughout 2025 as a special teamer and reserve safety, but when he was waived late in the year, the Carolina Panthers claimed him. Seattle nevertheless gave Bell a Super Bowl ring for his efforts . Seattle has had Ty Okada and Julian Love starting in tandem since Week 5, with Okada missing a month due to a…

stories.title: Officials who were bumped by reconfigured Week 10 schedule won't lose pay
stories.summary: The four officials who worked two games in Week 10 got paid accordingly.
stories.detail: The four officials who worked two games in Week 10 got paid accordingly . The officials who found themselves without an assignment after the deck was reshuffled due to the ground stop won't be docked. NFL Referees Association executive director Scott Green tells PFT that the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the NFL and the NFLRA "requires that all active officials including anybody out with an injury are guaranteed 16 games of pay during the regular season regardless if they work all 16 games." Of course, it's possible that the NFL will reconfigure upcoming assignments to balance out the total assignments, putting an official who was supposed to work a given weekend on a bye while assigning an official to work when the official was supposed to be off. (That's not something Green said; it's our own assessment of how the imbalance can be rectified.) Hopefully, that won't happen. Those who were supposed to work but didn't should get credit for the game, since they were prepared to show up and do the job. And those who worked when they weren't supposed to shouldn't lose the opportunity to work their otherwise normal schedule — unless they choose that. And the four who worked tw…

stories.title: The Rams’ season starts now
stories.summary: After a stretch of four winnable games, the real test starts now for Sean McVay’s Rams
stories.detail: The Los Angeles Rams dug themselves out of a 2-4 hole en route to 6-4. They put together a four-game win streak. On the surface it seems like their early season struggles have all been corrected. In reality, their last four opponents have a combined record of 11-26-1. Cardinals 3-7 Chargers: 1-8 Commanders: 3-5-1 Raiders: 4-6 It’s reasonable to look at the last month’s schedule and conclude we really learned nothing about the Rams. Of course, they should be given credit for keeping losing teams losing. Who are the Rams following their recent rash of injuries? What happens when stiffer competition slows LA’s run game and they must rely on an inconsistent and short-handed passing attack? The defense has stymied offenses of late. What happens when they face the likes of Jordan Love, Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy, and Dak Prescott in the coming weeks? One thing is still true: the Rams have three lives left in the NFC playoff picture It will take 10 wins to make the playoffs. In other words, they cannot take more than three losses moving forward without leaving their destiny up to factors outside of their control. When looking on the horizon, LA’s season effectively starts out of their …

stories.title: Chiefs worked out K Matt Prater on Tuesday
stories.summary: The Chiefs worked out free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday, according to the NFL's personnel notice.
stories.detail: The Chiefs worked out free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday, according to the NFL's personnel notice. The team already has two veteran kickers, with Harrison Butker on the active roster and Justin Tucker on the practice squad. Butker is only 7-of-19 on field goal attempts this season. His struggles prompted the Chiefs to sign Tucker on Oct. 28. Butker had no field goal attempts in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Falcons, but he did make all five extra points. Prater, 42, has kicked for the Falcons (2007), Broncos (2007-13), Lions (2014-20), Cardinals (2021-24) and Bills (2025) in his 19-year career. Last season for the Bills, Prater made 23-of-25 field goals and 46-of-49 extra points, including the postseason. The Chiefs also worked out tight end John FitzPatrick, defensive tackle Aaron Graves, defensive tackle Eric Johnson and defensive tackle J.R. Singleton. FitzPatrick signed to the practice squad.

stories.title: Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns acting like ‘second coach’ sign of fixed Mike Brown partnership
stories.summary: A once rocky partnership has evolved into a trusting and collaborative relationship between Karl-Anthony Towns and Mike Brown.
stories.detail: Karl-Anthony Towns' relationship with Mike Brown has improved since the start of their first season together. TORONTO — A once rocky partnership has evolved into a trusting and collaborative relationship between Karl-Anthony Towns and Mike Brown. Towns revealed Tuesday that Brown has been embracing his suggestions “like I’m a second coach,” which is a residual benefit of their success in the 2026 postseason. It’s amazing what a championship can do. “It’s more familiarity with the system and building that trust with Mike where he can trust me with things I see and say, which started in the playoffs,” Towns said. “So building off that this year. Having more input and him hearing me out.” Towns said he and the coach collaborate “a lot” during games. “Him trusting me like a second coach. Me and him are always coaching with each other in the game, looking at game plans and plays and maybe ideologies and things I see that can help our team win, especially in close games,” Towns said. “Working with him and coaching on the floor. It’s been great. It’s been fun.” Karl-Anthony Towns looks to make a play as Scottie Barnes defends during the Knicks-Raptors game on Nov. 17, 2026, in Toronto. N…

stories.title: Jose Alvarado making Knicks presence felt — even if he’s not on court
stories.summary: Without playing time, Jose Alvarado has channeled his energy into being the No. 1 Knicks supporter.
stories.detail: TORONTO — Without playing time, Jose Alvarado has channeled his energy into being the No. 1 Knicks supporter. The third-string point guard has been, by far, the most boisterous and engaged Knick on the bench despite being pulled from the rotation a couple of weeks ago . “I think it’s more how I was raised [by] my parents,” Alvarado said. “Treat people how you want to be treated. Sometimes the situation isn’t going to be what you want. You can’t control certain things and control what you can and that’s your attitude, your energy every day. So I try to do that. Jose Alvarado greets forward Mohamed Diawara as he walks back to the bench during the Knicks’ blowout win over the Bucks on Nov. 10, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. Charles Wenzelberg / New York Post “I’m human, I have days where it’s not going to be all lovey-dovey. But I always tell myself, ‘Whether I’m not playing or not, I got the best seats in the house.’ And I get to support my teammates. So I try to go with that mindset as best I can and my teammates allow me to be myself.” In a viral moment from Sunday’s victory over the Raptors , Alvarado was filmed comforting a visibly dejected Mikal Bridges, who was struggling and…

stories.title: Trail Blazers rule star Deni Avdija out vs. Timberwolves with sore foot
stories.summary: The Trail Blazers ruled out star Deni Avdija for Tuesday night's game against the Timberwolves due to a sore left foot.
stories.detail: MINNEAPOLIS -- Portland Trail Blazers star Deni Avdija will miss Tuesday's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves with a sore left foot. Avdija was listed as questionable on the injury report but attempted to warm up on the court before being ruled out. Avdija scored 27 points on 11 of 19 shooting with eight rebounds and four assists in Portland's 106-98 loss on Monday night in Minnesota. This will be his first missed game of the season. Portland is also missing Ja Morant (left hamstring) and Shaedon Sharpe (right meniscus).
